title: Design presets
description: Switch the look of a whole app, or of one part of it, with a few props: a preset (minerva, editorial, compact, touch) or the individual design axes density, radius, shadow and font scale. Works with SSR and nested scopes.

axes.title: Design axes
axes.text: The design axes are orthogonal to the color mode (theme) and the palette. Each one selects a block of design tokens through a data attribute; components read the tokens (control heights, paddings, radii, shadows, font sizes), so the whole library follows. A preset is a named combination of the four axes plus a default palette; explicit axes and an explicit palette win over the preset.
axes.preset: minerva: Minerva's default look. editorial: restrained and reading-oriented (editorial palette, comfortable density, small radius, subtle shadows, large type). compact: dense, data-heavy screens (compact density, small radius, small type). touch: consumer mobile apps (comfortable density with 44px minimum touch targets, large radius).
axes.density: Control heights and horizontal paddings (--control-height-*, --control-padding-x-*) and the padding of rows such as menu items, options and table cells (--row-padding-y / --row-padding-x), and the minimum size of touch targets (--touch-target-min: 24px compact, 32px standard, 44px comfortable).
axes.shadow: Elevation shadows --shadow-sm to --shadow-xl. standard keeps the shadows of the theme or palette.
axes.fontScale: Type scale: --font-size-* and the base / relaxed line heights. large is meant for reading.

root.title: Whole app
root.text: Set the props on the root ConfigProvider: it writes the non-standard axes as data attributes on <html> (and the preset's palette as data-palette), and restores <html> when it unmounts. useConfig().design returns the resolved axes.

ssr.title: Server rendering
ssr.text: The root provider applies the attributes after hydration. For a first paint with the right look, render them in the server HTML with designAttributes() from the server-safe minerva-design/theme-utils entry, and/or pass the same design to createThemeInitScript({ design }), which also uses the preset's palette as the default palette.

nested.title: Nested scopes
nested.text: A nested ConfigProvider inherits the design of its parent and applies its overrides to its subtree only: a display: contents wrapper and the portal container of the scope carry every design attribute, so modals, popovers and toasts rendered from the subtree get the same look. A nested preset resets every axis it does not set.

css.title: Using the tokens in your own CSS
css.text: The axes only change design tokens, so your own styles can use the same variables and stay consistent with the components. Per-component tweaks are available through each component's CSS variables (see the "CSS variables" section of every component page).

DesignOptions.description: Design axes chosen by the app; unset axes come from the preset.

props.name: preset
props.description: Named combination of the axes below and a default palette: "minerva" (default look), "editorial" (restrained, reading-oriented), "compact" (dense, data-heavy screens) or "touch" (consumer mobile apps: comfortable density with 44px touch targets, large radius)

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density of controls and rows

examples.title: Presets
examples.description: The same screen under each preset. A nested ConfigProvider scopes the preset to the demo; on the root provider it applies to the whole document.

snippets.source:
<ConfigProvider preset="compact">
  {/* dense admin screens */}
  <ConfigProvider preset="editorial">
    {/* an article preview: editorial look, portals (Modal, Popover...) included */}
  </ConfigProvider>
  <ConfigProvider radius="none">
    {/* inherits compact, only the radius changes */}
  </ConfigProvider>
</ConfigProvider>
